rationale: Both candidates independently rediscovered the substance of the sole ground-truth concern (trust_remote_code breaking kernels 0.13.x fallback), tracing it through commit history to confirm it was already dropped — strong recall for both. X's remaining findings (missing cache-hit/fallback test coverage, duplicated attribute-validation logic, per-repo lock granularity, retry-without-backoff) are all tightly grounded with quoted file/line evidence and several include concrete ```suggestion``` diffs, making them highly actionable and verifiable. Y covers similar ground (same test-gap finding, same stale-description finding) but adds a striking unverifiable claim ('I ran the code with a stubbed kernels module', 'verified against installed kernels 0.16.0 that get_kernel() raises ValueError') that reads as overclaimed execution evidence rather than static analysis grounded in the diff, which drags down precision even though the surrounding reasoning is plausible. Neither includes a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
